# Prior to running any code

Please download the data from
<https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/stefanoleone992/mutual-funds-and-etfs>,
and store the file within a data/ folder in the working directory. If
the data is already stored then please skip this step.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(car)
library(writexl)
source('tools.R')
```

## 1. Load and clean the data

Read only the two fund files.

```{r load-data}
# Read in the dataset
etfs <- read.csv("data/ETFs.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
mutualfunds <- read.csv("data/MutualFunds.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
```

Keep the ytd return and the columns needed for the nine predictors.
Blank entries are treated as missing (`NA`).

```{r clean-data}

#---------------------------------------------
# 1.1. Impute missing asset allocations
#---------------------------------------------

# ETFs
etf_asset_cols <- grep("^asset_", names(etfs), value = TRUE)
etfs <- impute_allocation(etfs, etf_asset_cols)

# Mutual funds
mutual_fund_asset_cols <- grep("^asset_", names(mutualfunds), value = TRUE)
mutualfunds <- impute_allocation(mutualfunds, mutual_fund_asset_cols)

#---------------------------------------------
# 1.2. Select regression columns
#---------------------------------------------

columns <- c(
  "fund_return_ytd",
  "fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio",
  "total_net_assets",
  "inception_date",
  "asset_stocks",
  "asset_bonds",
  "annual_holdings_turnover",
  "fund_price_earning_ratio",
  "fund_sector_technology"
)

filtered_etfs <- etfs[, columns]
filtered_mutualfunds <- mutualfunds[, columns]


#---------------------------------------------
# 1.3. Combine datasets
#---------------------------------------------

filtered_etfs$etf_indicator <- 1
filtered_mutualfunds$etf_indicator <- 0

funds <- rbind(filtered_etfs, filtered_mutualfunds)


#---------------------------------------------
# 1.4. Fill remaining missing ETF assets with 0
#---------------------------------------------

all_assets <- grep("^asset_", names(funds), value = TRUE)

# Exclude stocks and bonds
non_etf_assets <- setdiff(
  all_assets,
  c("asset_stocks", "asset_bonds")
)

for (col in non_etf_assets) {
  target_rows <- funds$etf_indicator == 1 & is.na(funds[[col]])
  funds[target_rows, col] <- 0
}


#---------------------------------------------
# 1.5. data engineering
#---------------------------------------------

# create fund age
funds <- funds %>%
  mutate(inception_date = as.Date(inception_date)) %>%
  filter(inception_date < as.Date("2021-01-01"))

funds$fund_age_years <- as.numeric(
  as.Date("2021-01-01") - funds$inception_date
) / 365.25

funds$inception_date <- NULL

# Represent P/E availability while retaining rows with a missing raw P/E
pe <- funds$fund_price_earning_ratio
pe_median <- median(pe, na.rm = TRUE)

funds$pe_reported <- as.integer(!is.na(pe))

funds$pe_centered_when_reported <-
  (ifelse(is.na(pe), pe_median, pe)) - pe_median


#---------------------------------------------
# 1.6. Remove incomplete observations
#---------------------------------------------

colSums(is.na(funds))

model_data <- funds[, !names(funds) %in% "fund_price_earning_ratio"]
model_data <- model_data[complete.cases(model_data), ]

# Compare observations before and after cleaning
table(funds$etf_indicator)
table(model_data$etf_indicator)

```

### Sample and missingness audit

```{r part2-eda-sample, echo=FALSE}
p2_group <- function(data) {
  factor(data$etf_indicator, levels = c(0, 1),
    labels = c("Mutual fund", "ETF"))
}
p2_counts <- rbind(
  "Eligible before complete-case filtering" = table(p2_group(funds)),
  "Main model sample" = table(p2_group(model_data)),
  "P/E reported in model sample" = table(p2_group(
    model_data[model_data$pe_reported == 1L, ]))
)
knitr::kable(cbind(p2_counts, Total = rowSums(p2_counts)))
round(100 * p2_counts[2, ] / p2_counts[1, ], 1)

p2_fields <- c("fund_return_ytd", "total_net_assets", "fund_age_years",
  "asset_stocks", "asset_bonds", "annual_holdings_turnover",
  "fund_price_earning_ratio", "fund_sector_technology",
  "fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio")
p2_missing <- lapply(split(funds[, p2_fields], p2_group(funds)),
  function(group) colSums(is.na(group)))
knitr::kable(do.call(cbind, p2_missing))
```

Allocation filling uses the unit-sum rule in `tools.R`. The missingness
table describes records after that step. The model uses a P/E reporting
indicator and centered P/E where reported. Unequal retention by fund type
is a reason to examine the analysis sample before generalizing.

## 2. Fit the model

```{r regression}
model <- lm(fund_return_ytd ~ total_net_assets +
    fund_age_years + asset_stocks + asset_bonds +
    annual_holdings_turnover +
    fund_sector_technology + pe_reported + pe_centered_when_reported + 
    fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio * etf_indicator,
  data = model_data
)
```

The ETF coefficient is the adjusted ETF–mutual fund difference at an expense
ratio of zero. The interaction coefficient is the difference between the two
expense-ratio slopes. This baseline uses the original return and asset scales.

## 3. Summary tables and tests

```{r}
# Describe fitted model
summary(model)
```

```{r}
# Describe cleaned dataset including potentially unused observations
summary(model_data)
```

```{r design-matrix}
# Standardized third moment: positive = right skew,
# negative = left skew. Undefined for constant columns
skewness <- function(x) {
  spread <- sqrt(mean((x - mean(x))^2))
  if (spread == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  mean(((x - mean(x)) / spread)^3)
}

design_summary <- model_data %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value),
    median = median(value),
    SD = sd(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    skewness = skewness(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

design_summary
```

```{r}
# 95% confidence interval
confint(model)
```

```{r}
# ANOVA test
intercept_only <- lm(fund_return_ytd ~ 1, data = model_data)
anova(intercept_only, model)
```

```{r}
# Test each predictor while accounting for all the others
drop1(model, test = "F")
```

```{r}
# The first column is the response; exclude it from predictor covariance
covariance_matrix <- cov(model_data[, -1])
knitr::kable(signif(covariance_matrix, 4))
```

The covariance diagonal runs from top left to bottom right and contains
variances. Covariances depend on units, so their sizes alone do not
measure collinearity. Four significant digits are used only to display
the table.

## 4. Graphs

```{r}
n <- nobs(model)
p <- model$rank
cd <- cooks.distance(model)
db <- dfbetas(model)
dfits <- dffits(model)
r <- rstudent(model)
h <- hatvalues(model)
```

```{r}
diagnostics <- data.frame(
  cooks = cd,
  dffits = dfits,
  dfbetas = apply(abs(db), 1, max),
  residuals = r,
  leverage = h
)

diagnostics$flags <-
  (cd > qf(0.5, p, n-p)) +
  (abs(dfits) > 2*sqrt(p/n)) +
  (apply(abs(db), 1, max) > 2/sqrt(n))

# Number of observations flagged how many influnces it has
table(diagnostics$flags)

subset(diagnostics, flags == 3)
```

```{r}
temp_model_data <- cbind(
  position = seq_len(nobs(model)),
  original_row = rownames(model.frame(model)),
  model.frame(model),
  diagnostics)

write_xlsx(temp_model_data, "model_data.xlsx")
```

```{r}
which(abs(dfits) > 2*sqrt((p)/n))
which(abs(db) > 2 / sqrt(n))
which(cd > qf(0.5, p, n - p))
vif(model) # check multicolinearity
```

```{r check-diagnostics, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
checks$diagnostics
```

## Part 2 exploratory model checks

These checks use the same fitted rows as the main regression. The team's
allocation and P/E preparation carries through to each candidate.

### Return summary by fund type

The summary describes the observed return distributions by fund type. It
uses the same records as the regression and complements the histogram and
boxplot in the existing diagnostic output.

```{r part2-eda-distribution, echo=FALSE}
p2_fitted_data <- model.frame(model)
p2_type <- p2_group(p2_fitted_data)
p2_ytd_pct <- 100 * p2_fitted_data$fund_return_ytd
p2_by_type <- split(p2_ytd_pct, p2_type)
knitr::kable(t(vapply(p2_by_type, function(y) {
  c(n = length(y), median_return_pct = median(y), sd_return_pct = sd(y))
}, numeric(3))), digits = 2)
```

### Standardized residuals and transformation trials

Compare candidate transformations on the same records. The natural log
compresses the asset scale. Adding 1 to the return gives positive inputs
for the square-root, log, and Box–Cox trials. Compare standardized residual
plots, the spread at the ends of the fitted-value range, and the lower
tail before choosing a scale.

```{r part2-eda-transforms, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
p2_residual_plots <- function(fit, label) {
  fitted_values <- fitted(fit)
  residual <- rstandard(fit)
  old <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  on.exit(par(old))
  plot(fitted_values, residual, pch = ".",
    xlab = "Fitted response", ylab = "Standardized residual", main = label)
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey50")
  lines(lowess(fitted_values, residual), col = "firebrick")
  qqnorm(residual, pch = ".")
  qqline(residual, col = "firebrick")
}

stopifnot(all(p2_fitted_data$total_net_assets > 0),
  all(1 + p2_fitted_data$fund_return_ytd > 0))
p2_log_assets <- update(model,
  . ~ . - total_net_assets + log(total_net_assets),
  data = p2_fitted_data, na.action = na.fail)
p2_sqrt <- update(p2_log_assets, sqrt(1 + fund_return_ytd) ~ .)
p2_log_return <- update(p2_log_assets, log(1 + fund_return_ytd) ~ .)

p2_residual_plots(model, "Original scales")
p2_residual_plots(p2_log_assets, "Log assets")
p2_residual_plots(p2_sqrt, "Square root of 1 + return")
p2_residual_plots(p2_log_return, "Log of 1 + return")

p2_positive <- update(p2_log_assets, I(1 + fund_return_ytd) ~ .)
p2_profile <- MASS::boxcox(p2_positive, lambda = seq(-2, 3, 0.05),
  plotit = TRUE, interp = FALSE)
p2_peak <- which.max(p2_profile$y)
p2_profile$x[p2_peak]
range(p2_profile$x[
  2 * (p2_profile$y[p2_peak] - p2_profile$y) <= qchisq(0.95, 1)])

p2_spread <- function(fit) {
  r <- rstandard(fit)
  value <- fitted(fit)
  band <- cut(value, quantile(value, 0:10 / 10), include.lowest = TRUE)
  spread <- tapply(r, band, sd)
  c(low_sd = unname(spread[1]), high_sd = unname(spread[10]),
    lower_tail = unname(quantile(r, 0.01)))
}
knitr::kable(rbind(raw = p2_spread(model), log_assets = p2_spread(p2_log_assets),
  sqrt_return = p2_spread(p2_sqrt), log_return = p2_spread(p2_log_return)),
  digits = 2)
```

### Same-row P/E comparison and allocation VIFs

Compare the two P/E terms jointly on the same rows. Dropping the reporting
indicator and the centered reported value together tests their contribution
as a block. The allocation VIFs come from regressing each allocation
column on the other design columns. Unequal residual variance calls
for caution in interpreting the conventional partial F test.

```{r part2-eda-pe-vif, echo=FALSE}
p2_without_pe <- update(model,
  . ~ . - pe_reported - pe_centered_when_reported,
  data = p2_fitted_data, na.action = na.fail)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(model.frame(p2_without_pe)),
  rownames(p2_fitted_data)))
anova(p2_without_pe, model)

p2_allocation_vif <- function(fit) {
  x <- model.matrix(fit)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(fit$rank == ncol(x) + 1L)
  names_to_check <- c("asset_stocks", "asset_bonds")
  vapply(names_to_check, function(name) {
    j <- match(name, colnames(x))
    aux <- lm(x[, j] ~ x[, -j, drop = FALSE])
    1 / (1 - summary(aux)$r.squared)
  }, numeric(1))
}
knitr::kable(rbind(raw = p2_allocation_vif(model),
  log_assets = p2_allocation_vif(p2_log_assets),
  without_pe = p2_allocation_vif(p2_without_pe)), digits = 2)
```

### Sensitivity to the largest Cook distance

Review leverage, standardized residuals, and Cook's distance using the
course screening thresholds. Refit without the highest-Cook row to see
how much the expense-ratio interaction changes. Use the result to describe
sensitivity while reviewing the source of the observation.

```{r part2-eda-influence, echo=FALSE}
p2_cook <- cooks.distance(model)
p2_largest <- which.max(p2_cook)
p2_cook_cutoff <- qf(0.5, model$rank, df.residual(model))
c(max_cook = max(p2_cook), cook_cutoff = p2_cook_cutoff,
  high_leverage = sum(hatvalues(model) > 2 * model$rank / nobs(model)),
  outlying_residual = sum(abs(rstandard(model)) > 4))

p2_fitted_data[p2_largest, c("etf_indicator", "fund_return_ytd",
  "fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio"), drop = FALSE]
p2_sensitivity <- lm(formula(model),
  data = p2_fitted_data[-p2_largest, ], na.action = na.fail)
p2_interaction <- "fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio:etf_indicator"
c(full = unname(coef(model)[p2_interaction]),
  without_row = unname(coef(p2_sensitivity)[p2_interaction]))
```


```{r}
# Box–Cox requires a positive response
stopifnot(all(1 + model.frame(model)$fund_return_ytd > 0))

# Keep the original model predictors; profile Box–Cox on 1 + return
p2_original_positive <- update(
  model,
  I(1 + fund_return_ytd) ~ .,
  data = model.frame(model),
  na.action = na.fail
)

bc_original <- MASS::boxcox(
  p2_original_positive,
  lambda = seq(-2, 3, by = 0.01),
  plotit = FALSE,
  interp = FALSE
)

lambda_hat <- bc_original$x[which.max(bc_original$y)]
cutoff <- max(bc_original$y) - qchisq(0.95, df = 1) / 2
lambda_ci <- range(bc_original$x[bc_original$y >= cutoff])

plot(bc_original$x, bc_original$y, type = "l",
     xlab = expression(lambda),
     ylab = "Profile log-likelihood",
     main = "Box–Cox profile: original predictors")
abline(h = cutoff, col = "red", lty = 2)
abline(v = lambda_hat, col = "blue", lty = 2)

lambda_hat
lambda_ci

```
